name: RpcInterceptor
purpose: Per call middleware that wraps a remote procedure invocation to read or mutate metadata, enforce deadlines and translate errors consistently across services.
invariants: Interceptors MUST call next exactly once per invocation unless they deliberately short circuit with a status.
Metadata keys that end with '-bin' ALWAYS carry binary values and CANNOT be compared as plain strings.
Keys starting with 'grpc-' are FORBIDDEN for user metadata because that prefix is reserved by the runtime.
A deadline propagated in ctx MUST NOT be extended by an interceptor; it SHALL only be shortened or respected.
Cancellation signals NEVER cross interceptor boundaries silently; every interceptor SHALL honor cancel or raise a cancellation error.
extension_contract: Plug an interceptor into the chain by registering it on the client or server channel at construction time; compose multiple interceptors as an ordered list where earlier entries sit closer to the network and later entries closer to the handler.

sources.locator: grpc.io/docs/guides/interceptors/ When to use, Client vs Server, Interceptor ordering sections

why_essential: Authentication, tracing, rate limiting and deadline discipline must apply uniformly to every RPC; an interceptor contract is where those concerns compose without editing each generated stub.
alternatives_considered: Decorators on each service method which duplicate logic per endpoint
Global monkey patching of the RPC client which breaks generated stubs on upgrade
